It was also stated that the applicant had taken the victim to a clinic of the other co-accused and the victim had taken alongwith her Rs.30,000/- and certain jewellery which the applicant took from the victim and left her alone.

A somewhat similar statement was given under Section 164 Cr.P.C. wherein the victim stated that she was called by the applicant and had gone with him on a motorcycle, however, subsequently, physical relations were formed and the applicant had refused to marry her.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant draws my attention to Annexure - 4 wherein the statement of one of the eyewitnesses is recorded who stated that the victim had gone alongwith the applicant on a motorcycle and no resistance was offered by the victim.
5. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.

6. Considering the fact that the entire case is premised on forming physical relations on false pretext of marriage and the age of the victim is around 35 years as stated in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., a clear case for bail is made out, particularly, when the applicant is in custody since 27.10.2023 and has no criminal antecedent.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.
